editorial:
Imagine living in Dublin years ago and deciding that your dream job is collecting horse poop. That is exactly what Quackser does, much to the annoyance of his family who just want him to get a real career. The vibe is lighthearted and quirky, focusing on this odd guy who is perfectly happy with his stinky business until he meets a cute American exchange student. She almost hits him with her car, and from there, they start a sweet, unlikely romance that adds a lot of heart to the story. It is a funny look at a guy who refuses to fit in with the crowd.

You will love how the movie balances the laughs with the sadness of a changing world. The acting is natural and makes you really root for Quackser, even if his job is gross. While the pace is a bit slow in the middle, the emotional payoff is worth it. If you can find it, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality, or you can check if it is available for renting on Apple TV. It is a great pick for a cozy night in if you like stories about underdogs.
endingExplained: Everything crashes down when the city bans horses, leaving Quackser without a job or a purpose. After his American girlfriend leaves for home, he feels totally lost. However, he eventually realizes that he cannot live in the past. He decides to move forward with his life and adapt to the modern world. The movie ends with him finding a new way to survive, showing that you can lose everything and still find a way to start over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves oddball characters and heartwarming stories.
